author_claim: Paul constructs an antithetical a-b-b-a chiasm in Romans 10:5a and 6a to contrast righteousness based on the Law with righteousness based on faith.
short_quote: This contrast is set in the form of a stark a-b-b-a chiasm in verses 5a and 6a
qualification: Paul contrasts the old righteousness attached to Moses with the new righteousness by faith speaking for itself.
notes: Oliver 2015:5 (Table 1). Contextual/ancillary pericope evidence (Leviticus 18:5 contrasted with Deuteronomy 30:11-12 in Rom 10:5a-6a); preserved without inflating B001-4 coverage.

author_claim: In quoting Deuteronomy 30:13, Paul alters Moses's phrase 'beyond the sea' to 'into the deep (abyss)' in Romans 10:7 to refer Christologically to Christ's resurrection.
short_quote: The ‘sea’ of Deuteronomy 30:13 is changed to the ‘deep (abyss)’ (Rm 10:7) that would better refer to bringing Christ from the dead.
qualification: The alteration specifically introduces Paul's explanatory gloss 'that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.'
notes: Oliver 2015:4 (Table 2, p. 5). Contextual/ancillary pericope evidence (Deuteronomy 30:13 in Rom 10:7); preserved without inflating B001-4 coverage.

author_claim: Paul does not cite Moses's thrice-repeated phrase 'so we/you may obey it' from Deuteronomy 30:12, 13, and 14 in Romans 10:6-8, yet implicates those words in his own context.
short_quote: Paul does not cite these words, but implicates them in his own context.
qualification: Oliver states that Moses repeated 'so we/you may obey it' three times to show the Law should be obeyed (fn. 9) and notes that partial citation with interpretive glosses was a common Jewish expositional approach (citing Hart, Dunn, and Kruse).
notes: Oliver 2015:4 (Table 2, p. 5; Prompt 2 [5], Table 2 in [6]). Contextual/ancillary pericope evidence (Deuteronomy 30:12-14); preserved without inflating B001-4 coverage.

author_claim: Paul derives the word-pair 'mouth' and 'heart' directly from Deuteronomy 30:14 in Romans 10:8b to construct the interlocking double chiasm in Romans 10:9-10.
short_quote: The 1-2-3-4 and 4-3-2-1 combinations of verses 9 and 10 are therefore already present in verse 8 as a 2-4-3-1 combination.
qualification: In verse 8b Paul introduces the verbal term κηρύσσομεν, which is replaced by ὁμολογέω in verses 9-10 to denote public proclamation.
notes: Oliver 2015:9 (Figures 2 & 3). Printed '4-3-2-1' wraps across lines on p. 9 as '4-3-2-\n1' (verified via pdftotext -layout; pdftotext without -layout strips the end-of-line hyphen as '4-3-21'). Contextual/ancillary pericope evidence; preserved without inflating B001-4 coverage.

author_claim: In Romans 10:11-13, Paul introduces four statements with γάρ to assert the universality of God's salvation through universal terms such as πᾶς (in vv. 11 & 13) and κύριος πάντων (in v. 12).
short_quote: Paul asserts the universality of God’s salvation, with words or phrases such as πᾶς (vv. 11 & 13) and κύριος πάντων (v. 12)
qualification: The verb καταισχύνω links back to ἐπαισχύνομαι in Romans 1:16, substantiating the removal of shame through the gospel. Oliver cites Bechtler (1994:306) without arguing text-critically that Paul altered LXX Isa 28:16 by adding πᾶς.
notes: Oliver 2015:7 (Table 1, p. 5). Shared direct evidence for B001-4 (Rom 10:11 / Isa 28:16) and B001-5 (Rom 10:13 / Joel 2:32).

author_claim: Paul cites Joel 2:32 in Romans 10:13 as a scriptural crescendo confirming that oral calling on the Lord's name results in eschatological salvation.
short_quote: It is the ‘something-being-said’ (in this case a repetition of the verb he has just utilised in verse 12) that results in σωτηρίαν.
qualification: The future passive verb σωθήσεται in verse 13 mirrors σωθήσῃ in verse 9, confirming oral invocation alongside faith as necessary. Primary-text comparison (P01F/P03F): Rom 10:13 quotes the core clause of LXX Joel 3:5a (πᾶς ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται) while omitting introductory καὶ ἔσται and adding γάρ; Oliver's heraldic interpretation is distinct from primary Greek textual facts.
notes: Oliver 2015:10 (Table 1, p. 5). Direct B001-5 evidence (Joel 2:32 / LXX 3:5).

author_claim: Paul uses the citation of Joel 2:32 in Romans 10:13 as a rhetorical pivot linking the personal confession of verses 9-10 with the missionary sequence in Romans 10:14-15.
short_quote: In Romans 10:14–15 Paul elaborates on verse 13 (citing a part of Is 52:7), emphasising his calling as an apostle, bringing the message orally
qualification: In verses 14-15, Paul reverses the verb sequence (call -> believe -> hear -> preach) to illustrate the missionary chain.
notes: Oliver 2015:5 (and pp. 10-11). Direct B001-5 evidence (Joel 2:32 as hinge between inner confession and outward heraldic mission).

author_claim: Except for verse 12 and the chiastic confession in verses 9-10, Romans 10:5-13 consists of Old Testament citations, creating the impression that Paul encased his words in Scriptures to give them greater prominence.
short_quote: It leaves the impression that, besides the use of the (double) chiasm, Paul has encased these words with Scriptures so as to highlight it more or to give it more prominence
qualification: Oliver hedges this structural observation ('It leaves the impression that...'); the encasing citations include Lev 18:5, Hab 2:4, Deut 9:4, Deut 30:12-14, Isa 28:16 (B001-4), and Joel 2:32 (B001-5).
notes: Oliver 2015:3 (Table 1, p. 5; Figure 1, p. 4). Contextual/ancillary pericope-level structural framing; preserved without inflating B001-4 coverage.

author_claim: In Romans 10:11, Paul uses the verb καταισχύνω to link back to ἐπαισχύνομαι in Romans 1:16, identifying both as references to LXX Isaiah 28:16.
short_quote: In verse 11 Paul uses the verb καταισχύνω, linking this passage back to Romans 1:16 where he uses the verb ἐπαισχύνομαι (both as references to Is 28:16 LXX).
qualification: Oliver cites Jewett (2007:138) on removing human shame and classifies v. 11 as citing prophetic words of Is 28:16 (LXX) (p. 4; Table 1, p. 5), without performing an MT-vs-LXX text-critical collation.
notes: Oliver 2015:3 (also p. 4; Table 1, p. 5). Direct B001-4 locus evidence (Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16).

author_claim: Oliver qualifies G. Aho's proposal that Isaiah 28:16 in Romans 10:11 stipulates the way of righteousness by faith is meant for all as potentially too subjective a reading within this pericope.
short_quote: are stipulating that ‘the way of righteousness by faith is meant for all’. This could be a too subjective reading of the verse within this pericope.
qualification: Oliver distinguishes Aho's (1981:308) thematic inference about Isaiah 28:16 itself from Paul's explicit universality argument in vv. 11-13 (p. 7, citing Bechtler 1994:306).
notes: Oliver 2015:3, fn. 5. Direct B001-4 methodological qualification on Isaiah 28:16.
